flyoverSteps.reproductionConfidence: high: production geometry/support regressions reproduce both causes
cause: Horizontal lane-marking boxes on slopes produced visible lips and intersections with the asphalt.
Clamped segment endpoints behaved as invisible flat ledges. Nearest-height selection could hold the old height until the car dropped to the next segment.
Legacy generated profiles included a 6.8 m climb in about 9 m; all-source audit found 1,398 segments above a 10% grade.
repair: A shared runtime model extends eased estimated approaches along connected roads. Original XY vertices, IDs and connectivity remain; collinear samples improve vertical curves.

Actual finite asphalt triangles determine car support, including bend and elevated-junction patches. Continuous uphill/downhill contact does not repeatedly detach or trigger landing slowdowns. Body pitch follows the grade.

Lane paint is a thin upward-facing surface following asphalt triangles, with a stronger depth bias than the asphalt. Browser inspection caught the initial paint disappearing under the road bias and corrected it.

Canonical grade patches reach both RoadGraph and streamed tile workers; road-bound pickup/drop heights follow the same model. Same-level road candidates can agree on stop height without inventing a road identity.
flyoverSteps.limit: These are model heights, not surveyed real-world flyover gradients. Three small isolated estimated peaks were lowered to satisfy protected underpass constraints; major plateaus and Durgam deck height remain.

guidance.reproductionConfidence: high for lateral spur, timed rebuild and false grade transfer; broader city route quality remains partial coverage
cause: Route points began at the actual car and jumped sideways to a fixed centreline/lane, especially on ORR outer lanes.
A full route/mesh rebuild every 1.5–4 seconds visibly moved the entry and could choose another route.
The old binary elevated-node suffix could connect source nodes at different elevated heights.
repair: Retain valid route choice and advance its leading point every frame; recalculate after actual departure, recovery/landing, missing route edges or useful new incomplete-route connectivity.
Keep normalized one-way lane position across split/reversed road records. Prefer the actual supported road and verify physical side on divided roads.
Use actual source/target heights and distinct height levels at graph nodes.
Halve road ribbon width from 1.4 m to 0.7 m, minimap stroke 7 to 3.5 and full-map stroke 6 to 3.

Apply small sampled corner fillets only on loaded same-grade pavement with player-sized wall/facade clearance; retain legal corners where a fillet is unverified or blocked. New routes fade in, with no coordinate morph through obstacles.
Reuse dynamic GPU storage and share the same route choice with map displays. Minimap now uses the actual Red/Blue/Green metro palette too.
guidance.retainedOpenEvidence: PT-005 remains suspected in the historical registry. This repair covers median/clearance and lane geometry regressions; it does not retroactively claim the original historical scene was reproduced and closed.

mobile.repair: Four equal circular arrows replace GO/BRAKE and rectangular steering controls. Normal size 70×70 px; short landscape 58×58 px, matching the prior brake target size. Up/down at right; FLY/ACT above left/right. Safe areas, accessible names, pointer ownership, release/reset behavior and gyro hiding retained. Prompts reserve the two-row layout.
